Draw it as an irregular patch a shade paler and shinier than the skin around it, with raised, puckered ridges and no readable shape. It is not red, dark or ink-like, and it is not a tattoo, cross, rosette, monogram, letter or numeral. Draw one brand only.

panels.reason: The Maravar look (bare-headed, dun and dark-brown ponies, no greys) is the Chapter 7 lock (CH07 2.1, 3.4, 7.3) and is missing from the prompt. The fishermen's dress follows the author's 2026-09-30 decision (bare-chested with a shoulder cloth, plain dyed colours, no checks). The sheet shows rolled sleeves. Dropped the Madurai sentence because the madurai_troop continuity line in the prompt already says it. Reworded 'no mark on either arm' so it hides the brand without denying it. Separate pipeline note: the lettering block asks for space 'preferably in the upper part', but cover_crop trims the height toward the faces for a 3:1 strip, so caption space may need to sit in the middle band.

panels.addendum: This is its own standalone frame. Fill the whole canvas edge to edge with the hut scene only: no beach, no second picture, no border or frame. panels.reason: layout_fit treats insets as separate panels that share rows, so the 'Small inset, lower corner of 1.1' wording does risk a picture-in-picture. But 'places it beside 1.1' was inaccurate, so I removed it. The evening hut invites a glass lantern (failure mode 7). Fisherman dress follows the author's decision. The red-smear risk is failure mode 8. The sheet draws a drop below the lobe, and Ch4 REVIEW.md rejected the dangling ear ornament four times (rows 2.2, 2.3, 4.3, 5.5).

panels.addendum: 'Bright' turbans means sunlit white: every Madurai lancer's high-wrapped turban is white or off-white, and none is coloured. The Maravar riders are bare-headed, on small dun and dark-brown ponies. Nagoji's grey is the only grey horse.
panels.reason: 'Bright high-wrapped turbans' in the script really can pull coloured turbans against the white or off-white lock. The Maravar head and pony lock from Ch7 is missing. Cut the horse colours and jama, which the continuity line already gives. Also cut the shield-emblem sentence: it is speculative and is not a confirmed failure mode.

panels.reason: A grey riderless horse would read as Nagoji's mount, and fixing it as a Madurai charger does not change the story. The Maravar lock is missing. Dusk warm light on bandages is a real blood-read risk (failure mode 8). Removed the Madurai dress sentence, which repeats the continuity line.

panels.addendum: Frame from the grey's shoulder up: Nagoji's torso and head, with the horse's neck and head, at one side of the frame. Ramayyan sits cross-legged on a high verandah plinth, so his head is close to level with Nagoji's. Both faces sit in the middle half of the image height, with the column small behind them. Leave plain wall or sky beside the faces, inside that same middle band, for the lettering. The grey has a quilted Indian saddle and a plain leather bridle. The palm-leaf bundle is blank pale leaf.
panels.reason: A mounted man and a seated man cannot both keep their faces in the middle half of a 3:1 strip unless the staging is controlled (failure mode 10). The script's 'level with him' supports the high plinth. I softened 'same eye height' to 'close to level' to avoid odd geometry. Moved the lettering space into the middle band, because cover_crop trims the top. Shortened the leaf wording to 'blank' so it does not name scratches or rows that could invite marks.
